what: Implement the SCEM and Cosine method on the Armenia data
title: SCEM_example
code: results = SCEM(armenia,bandwidth = -0.33) cosine = makeFits(armenia,method ="OLS")   rownames(cosine) = 1:nrow(cosine)  results$results$Cosine = cosine$birth dif = abs(results$results$Cosine - results$results$Season) results$results$Difference = apply(cbind(dif,(1-dif)),1,min) results$results$R = cosine$Pearson rrr.a = results$results[order(results$results$Cluster),]  # Storing the birth seasonality estimates from two methods c.armenia = results$results$Cosine s.armenia = results$results$Season

what: Prepare relevant plots for the above analysis
title: SCEM_example
code: # Plotting the estimates of birth seasonality from the two methods plot(c.armenia,s.armenia,xlim = c(0,1),ylim = c(0,1),pch = 19) abline(0,1) legend("topleft","Tsaghkahovit") title(xlab = "estimated birth seasonality from cosine method",ylab = "estimated birth seasonality from SCEM",outer = TRUE, line = 2) # Plotting the graphs of the clusters for Armenia data  gnum = max(results$results$Cluster) oldpar = par(mar=c(1.5,1.5,1,1), mfrow=c(2,2),oma = c(4, 4, 1, 1)) for(i in 1:gnum){   if(length(results$groups[[i]])>1){     cc = as.character()     plot(c(0,40),c(-14,0),type = "n",axes = T,xlab = "",ylab = "",xlim = rev(range(c(0,40))))     for(j in 1:length(results$groups[[i]])){       tt = armenia[[results$groups[[i]][j]]]       lines(tt$distance,tt$oxygen,lty = j)       cc = c(cc,paste(tt$lab[1],tt$ID[1],sep = ""))     }     legend("topleft",legend = cc,lty = c(1:j),lwd = 2)   } } title(xlab = "distance from CEJ (mm)",ylab = expression(delta^18*O[VPDB]*' (per mil)'),outer = TRUE, line = 2) par(oldpar)

what: Use Armenia data to show the sensitivity to initialization (for Cosine method)
title: SCEM_example
code: # Fix the initial values of amplitude and intercept amp = seq(1,10,by=0.5) int = seq(-25,0,by=0.5)  # Find the estimate of birth seasonality, period, delay and the R^2 for all cases cosfit.birth = array(0,dim = c(length(amp),length(int),length(armenia))) cosfit.period = array(0,dim = c(length(amp),length(int),length(armenia))) cosfit.delay = array(0,dim = c(length(amp),length(int),length(armenia))) cosfit.R = array(0,dim = c(length(amp),length(int),length(armenia))) for (i in 1:length(amp)){   for (j in 1:length(int)){     dd = makeFits(armenia,amp[i],int[j],method="initial")     cosfit.birth[i,j,] = dd$birth     cosfit.period[i,j,] = dd$X     cosfit.delay[i,j,] = dd$x0     cosfit.R[i,j,] = dd$Pearson   } } birth.means = numeric(length(armenia)) birth.var = numeric(length(armenia)) for (i in 1:length(armenia)){   birth.means[i] = mean(c(cosfit.birth[,,i]))   birth.var[i] = var(c(cosfit.birth[,,i])) }  # Plots of the model fits to show the sensitivity to initial conditions  oldpar2= par(mfrow = c(1,2),mar = c(4,4,1,1)) plot(birth.means,sqrt(birth.var),xlab = "mean of birth season",ylab = "standard deviation",pch = 19) hist(c(cosfit.R^2),25,freq = F,xlab = "R-squared value",main = "") par(oldpar2)

title: Splitting-Coalescence-Estimation Method
text: introduce improved methods statistically assessing birth seasonality intra-annual variation \(\delta^{18}O\) faunal tooth enamel. first method propose new idea uses nonparametric clustering procedure group individuals similar time series data estimate birth seasonality based clusters. method efficient across different scenarios, especially less tooth row preserved. new approach offers high level statistical rigor flexibility dealing time series data produced intra-individual sampling isotopic analysis. One can use function SCEM() implement method. using SCEM estimate birth seasonality values, important keep two things mind: 1) non-parametric clustering procedure valid kind time series data, estimation birth seasonality semi-parametric return valid results non-sinusoidal time series; 2) simulation study suggests SCEM provides accurate estimates birth seasonality second molars long tooth enamel 50% original crown height present (Chazin et al.2019, Table 1). second method estimates input parameters use previously-developed parametric approach (Tornero et al., 2013). relevant code approach makeFits_OLS(), makeFits_initial() code implement method given initial conditions two parameters. latter can used show disadvantage existing approach. One can use function makeFits() generate parametric birth seasonality estimates using either initialization. Example implementing methods data (provided ‘armenia’) can found vignettes folder https://chazind.github.io/SCEM/. functions repository used internally -mentioned functions.

what: Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) for a partition. — EBIC
title: Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) for a partition. — EBIC
text: function calculates extended version BIC, computed using particular weighted average total residual sum squares number clusters. SCEM uses following equation BIC partition: MathJax = {output: {font: "mathjax-newcm", fontPath: "../../mathjaxr/doc/mathjax/font",}};  \[BIC(P) = (np)\log \left\lbrace\frac{RSS(P)}{np}\right\rbrace + |P|(B_{n}^{-1}-1) \log(nB_{n}),\] \(RSS(P) = \sum_{q=1}^{Q} RSS(S_q)\). sample size individual time series (.e. number observations) denoted \(n\), dealing archaeological data, time series data set number observations. order reasonable representative value sample size, chosen use natural arithmetic mean \(n=(n_1+\dots+n_p)/p\). \((B_{n}^{-1}-1)\log(nB_{n})\) tuning parameter places penalty number clusters (also note term \(nB_{n}\)). Using different tuning parameter \(\gamma_{n}\) place \((B_{n}^{-1}-1)\log(nB_{n})\) allows stronger weaker penalties number clusters.

Also, following definition, assumes value \(x(t)/X\) maximizes \(z(t)\) estimated birth seasonality. Birth seasonality estimated using combined data individuals single cluster, birth seasonality estimates individuals cluster based individual estimates length tooth crown (\(X_{k}\)). detailed description algorithm, please see Chazin et al. 2019, Supplemental Materials 1.
